entries.cue: Transparent pipe visibly leaking red liquid into a puddle.
entries.prior: New composition using docs/visual-cue-catalog.json#leaking-container and the red-fluid leak ingredient from docs/chapter-1-broadened-cue-audit.md#hemorrhage-control, also recorded in Chapter5.
entries.reason: Keeps the familiar leak without the prior cue's clamp, because control is not the selected word. Not an anatomical leak site, blood-loss estimate, injury mechanism or procedure. Newly recorded adaptation, not a new primitive.

entries.cue: Nearly empty transparent reservoir connected in a closed circulation loop, with red liquid low at its bottom.
entries.reason: Reuses the established low-volume composition. Does not diagnose a cause, equate all low volume with hemorrhage, encode a threshold or recommend a fluid.

entries.cue: Shivering study mannequin beside a conspicuous block of ice.
entries.reason: Familiar cold state is sufficient at the learned category level; no need for all name syllables. Ice is an assigned cold token, not a cause, clinical sign requirement, temperature threshold or treatment instruction.

entries.cue: Conspicuous lemon used as the learned acid token.
entries.reason: Existing sour-fruit acidity token supports a broad learned association; it does not uniquely separate acidosis from every acid-related term. No dietary causation, acid-base definition, laboratory value, mechanism or corrective treatment is encoded.

entries.cue: Oxygen-cylinder character presenting an empty open wallet to a waiting bill collector.
entries.prior: New composition; oxygen-cylinder ingredient also appears in docs/chapter-7-cue-audit.json#hyperbaric-oxygen-therapy.
entries.reason: Familiar owing/debt situation can bridge the phrase without clinical explanation. Lesson context must teach debt rather than mere poverty or purchase. No oxygen dose, repayment timing, physiologic definition or clinical endpoint is supplied.

entries.cue: Heart character sprinting with conspicuous speed streaks.
entries.reason: Economical familiar fast-plus-heart association, not a forced tacky rebus. Running is metaphorical; no rhythm diagnosis, rate threshold, exercise recommendation or cause of a rapid pulse is encoded.

entries.cue: Air balloon outside a lung but inside a transparent chest shell.
entries.reason: Reuses the established spatial token. The selected unqualified word occurs separately from tension pneumothorax; no tension subtype, mechanism, diagnostic criterion or intervention is encoded. Balloon is not a literal foreign body.

entries.cue: Red liquid around a lung inside a transparent chest shell.
entries.reason: Reuses prior blood/chest category token; not a volume estimate, source of bleeding, clinical mechanism, diagnosis or drainage instruction. Distinguish liquid from the pneumothorax balloon within a shared lesson.

entries.cue: A conspicuous cluster of clear crystals.
entries.cue_scope: Crystal- name fragment in fluid vocabulary context
entries.reason: Same-batch reuse rather than another discovery; plural does not need a new picture or extra pitcher. Full class identity comes from lesson context, not visible fluid crystals, formulation or administration instructions.

entries.cue: Recognizable red-cell study tokens tightly packed together in a transparent bag.
entries.prior: New composition; red-cell teaching tokens also occur in docs/chapter-10-cue-audit.json#pancytopenia, there as a nearly empty category bin.
entries.reason: Visible packing supports the ordinary phrase with learned cell tokens. Not a product specification, concentration, storage standard, transfusion indication or claim that all bagged blood is this component.

entries.cue: Bank vault holding recognizable blood bags.
entries.reason: Reuses the existing bank/vault word association. Plural wording does not require multiple vaults. Not inventory, availability, product selection, storage or handling instructions.

entries.cue_scope: Cross plus matches name bridge in blood context
entries.reason: Reuses the same bridge despite source hyphenation. Not a compatibility-testing method or result; matches are word tokens, not heat, fire or handling instructions.

entries.cue: Frost-covered transparent bag of pale yellow fluid beside a snowflake token.
entries.prior: New composition sharing docs/visual-cue-catalog.json#cold-ice as a cold-state primitive; no prior whole-phrase cue located in checked banks/workshops.
entries.reason: Familiar frozen appearance can support a taught product-category association without forcing fresh or plasma into a rebus. Color and frost alone do not distinguish every blood component. Not a product-identification guide, storage temperature, thawing method, compatibility rule or use instruction.

entries.cue: Small stack of miniature dinner plates.
entries.cue_scope: Plate- plus smallness learned name bridge
entries.reason: Familiar little plates can bridge the name without exact syllable recovery. Not actual cell morphology, a cell count, clinical function, product quantity or a clotting mechanism.
Reuses established calcium ingredient identity, not a new drug-specific cue. Not a calcium level, formulation, deficiency, transfusion relationship or replacement instruction.

entries.cue_scope: Full medication name not economically cued here
entries.reason: Carries forward the prior hold. Acid-family lemon alone would not add a useful medication-name association beyond the retained broad acid token; no forced train/exam/acid syllable chain proposed. Hold is provisional, not proof that no useful bridge exists.

entries.cue: Thick putty stretched into a strand between two hands, with a short strand recoiling beside it.
entries.reason: Familiar putty behavior offers a learned material-category bridge without reconstructing every syllable. Recoil may need taught interpretation. Not a clot model, assay trace, device specification, test interpretation or statement about treatment benefit.
